newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate firms, baht falls late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate firms, baht falls late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate rose to 13.00-13.25 percent in late trade on Monday from 12.00 percent earlier and 11.00-11.50 late on Friday as a result of heavy buying of the dollar, dealers said.

"Most major local banks offered a small amount of funds to the market today," said one dealer at a foreign bank. "They were keeping their money to speculate on the dollar in the foreign exchange market."
The baht fell to 25.521-25.526 to the dollar late from 25.510-25.513 early due to the U.S. unit's sharp rise against the Japanese yen, dealers said.

"There seems to be no resistance for the dollar against other major currencies right now," said one currency dealer. "There will be more buying of the dollar as a lot of dealers were apparently short of dollars."
The one-month baht/dollar swap premium was quoted at 9.00/10.00 satangs per dollar late, unchanged from early morning.
The mid-rate was fixed at 25.49 to the dollar against 25.47 on Friday. The mid-rate of 25.49 is the lowest level since January 26, 1994 when the mid-rate was fixed at 25.50.
